page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth, recording read-only small block cached speeds of 7387.52 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds of 210.01 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations scale efficiently, as evidenced by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top decile, processing 133.04 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics and text processing fall into the average tier, and small-model text generation shows poor relative performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8gb.16xlarge offers high compute density and memory throughput per resource unit, typical of the ARM64 Graviton architecture. The lack of local storage requires external block storage, which represents a structural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and medium-to-large LLM text generation tasks.
